key_insight: Multimodal machine learning modestly predicted primary resistance to anti-PD-(L)1 therapy in advanced NSCLC, outperforming PD-L1 and TMB in first-line chemo-immunotherapy but not PD-L1 in later-line therapy.
clinical_relevance: The signature could support research into pretreatment resistance stratification, but these findings do not establish readiness for treatment selection.
method: Prospective biomarker profiling across 17 centres, integrating clinical, laboratory, circulating immune, vascular, tumour immune and molecular data.
Benchmarked 360 feature-selection and machine-learning pipelines using .632 optimism correction.
Identified an 18-feature signature including stromal regulatory T cells, circulating transitional B cells and routine laboratory variables.
evidence_signal: Among 435 evaluable patients, 39.5% had primary resistance; corrected AUROC was 0.69 in both treatment settings, with first-line PPV of 0.51 versus 0.36 for PD-L1 and 0.35 for TMB.
watch_item: Discrimination remained modest, and the abstract reports internal optimism correction rather than independent external validation.
paper_title: Multimodal profiling for prediction of primary resistance to anti-PD-(L)1 therapy in advanced non-small-cell lung cancer: the prospective PIONeeR biomarkers study
